title.narrative: Support to conflict affected IDPs recently returned or relocated in Tiru District, Afar Regional State

description.narrative:
ltpgtltbrgt lt/pgtltpgtThe proposed project aims to address the urgent needs of 34,872 people - 80% IDP returnees, and 20% host community/non-IDP returnees in Teru, Afar regional state through a comprehensive and integrated multi-sector response. The targeted locations have experienced conflicts, environmental disasters, high food insecurity, and a residual caseload of IDP returnees. To effectively address these challenges, an area-based approach will be adopted, focusing on holistic assistance, participatory engagement, and geographical targeting.lt/pgt ltpgtWith a grant request of USD $1,000,000.00, the project will allocate funds to key sectors based on their prioritization identified in the allocation, and rapid assessment conducted by IR to inform this application and the expected level of impact of the intervention. Accordingly, Agriculture (30%), Multi-Purpose Cash (30%), WASH (25%), and Protection (15%) have been identified as critical sectors to improve food security and livelihoods, basic needs, water and sanitation conditions, and protection mechanisms. The project will address IDP returnees as its primary targets while supporting the non-DIP returnee - local communities to the extent possible as many of the IDP returnees are living within this community. This was confirmed through a rapid needs assessment conducted by IRE in Teru during this application preparation. The design of this proposal is participatory and the prioritization was done fully in consultation with local government and community representatives.lt/pgt ltpgtltspangtltbrgtlt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtltspangtThe overall objective of the project is to contribute to supporting the voluntary and dignified return of the most vulnerable IDPs through an integrated multi-sector approach. This will be achieved through increased access to income, improved water and sanitation facilities, and enhanced protection mechanisms. The project will conduct a detailed needs verification assessment, provide emergency livestock supportlt/spangtltspangt, provide multi-purpose cash transfers, rehabilitate water lt/spangtstrategicltspangt lt/spangtltspangtschemes lt/spangtltspangtand upgrade to solar energy, provision of WaSH NFI, hygiene and sanitation lt/spangtcampaignltspangt, and implement protection activities. The project will reach a total of 34, 872 (27, 872 most vulnerable people IDP returnees and 7000 host communities) through this intervention for its ten months implementation period.lt/spangtlt/pgt ltpgtThrough close monitoring, evaluation, and documentation of project activities and outcomes, the project will ensure accountability, learning, and the generation of best practices for future programming. By engaging with relevant stakeholders and leveraging participatory design and implementation, the project will maximize its impact and contribute to the sustainable recovery of the affected communities in Teru, Afar. lt/pgt
